name: Oman
headline: Oman: +2.4% growth in 2025, 1.0% inflation, debt 35% of GDP
sections: Oman is a $109 billion economy (2025), the world's 72nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.4% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $42K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.4% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 2.5% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.3% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 13.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 35% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 68% in 2020. The general government balance is +0.6% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −1.1% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 115% of GDP (2024), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 6.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 29% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 80.2 years (2024). Population: 5.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
